title: eBay Says No to GameStop's $56 Billion Buyout Offer
summary: Imagine a smaller store trying to buy a much bigger one. That's what happened this week. GameStop, the video game retailer, offered $56 billion to buy eBay, the huge online marketplace. But eBay said no. It called the offer "neither credible nor attractive." That means eBay thinks the deal isn't believable or good. eBay is about four times bigger than GameStop by market value. Its stock has gone up 201% since its current CEO, Jamie Iannone, took over six years ago. GameStop's CEO, Ryan Cohen, surprised everyone with the bid. He had a letter from TD Bank promising $20 billion in loans. But eBay worries the combined company wouldn't get a good credit rating. Without that, the deal might fall apart. Cohen said he could cut costs and use GameStop's 600 U.S. stores to help eBay compete with Amazon. But analysts point out eBay already makes more profit per sale than GameStop. Cohen became famous in 2021 when he helped cause a "short squeeze" that hurt some big investors. Now, he owns 5% of eBay and might ask shareholders to vote on the deal. But that's hard to do. eBay's board says the company is doing fine on its own. The stock market seems to agree: eBay's shares are trading far below Cohen's offer price of $125. For now, the two companies will stay separate.
why_it_matters: This story shows how even big companies battle over who's in charge, and it teaches us that size and a strong plan often matter more than a bold offer.

background_read: GameStop (a video game store chain with many physical shops) became famous in 2021 when its stock price shot up unexpectedly due to a 'short squeeze'.
eBay (one of the world's largest online marketplaces, where people buy and sell everything from toys to cars) has been growing steadily under its current CEO, Jamie Iannone.
Ryan Cohen (the billionaire investor who took over GameStop) had tried to shake up other companies before. TD Bank (a large Canadian bank) supported his plan with a big loan promise.
Article_Structure: WHO: GameStop (the video-game retailer) and eBay (the huge online marketplace), led by Ryan Cohen and Jamie Iannone
WHAT: GameStop made a $56 billion buyout offer, but eBay called it not credible and turned it down
WHERE: This all happened in the U.S. stock and business world
WHY: eBay believes it is much bigger and stronger on its own, and doubts the deal would work because of credit worries

perspectives.description: They believe combining the two companies could cut costs and use GameStop's stores to take on Amazon.
They think the offer doesn't make sense because eBay already earns more profit per sale and can grow on its own.
They point out that the merged company might have a bad credit rating, which would make the whole deal shaky and hard to finish.
